newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW-S.Electric mulls payout to holders.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-S.Electric mulls payout to holders.

text.p: British regional electricity company Southern Electric Plc said on Thursday it was mulling a number of options -- including a possible special dividend or share buyback -- to return some 180 million stg to shareholders.
Marchant said Southern Electric did not currently expect to try any mergers or acquisitions after its previous tie-up plans were thwarted twice this year.
"Given the (regulatory) environment and the political scene we're facing, we do not believe that a deal is currently feasible for us," he said.

"But we do not need to do a deal. We've got good growth prospects in all our core businesses and we're committed to growing organically," he added, noting the company's plan to invest 700 million stg over five years in its network.

The company's expansion plans included beefing up its supply business and making additional investments in two embedded generation plants. Proposals for a further three generation sites in its region were well-advanced, he said.
Marchant added that the firm expected to agree early next year to an electricity supply deal similar to its recent 15-year agreement with nuclear power generator British Energy Plc .
"The principal advantage is that it gives us secure access to competitively-priced generation," he said.
He declined to give details of the expected deal.
Southern Electric's shares rose 4.0p to 691.5 by 0945 GMT.
